source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Enable Scalable and Reliable Circuit Identification in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different circuit-identification method based on sparse autoencoder codes, then evaluates an identified GPT-2 Small IOI circuit by replacing activations outside it and measuring IOI performance. It also compares circuit-recovery AUCs across methods and ablation types.
record.gate_note: The study reports IOI circuit performance, IOI circuit-identification AUCs, and IOI-specific sensitivity analyses. It also includes results on Greater-than, Docstring, Tracr, and induction; those do not directly test the IOI claim versions here. The head-class roles are described and visualized, but are not individually tested by role-specific patching.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates the canonical 26-head IOI circuit's faithfulness under subject-swap corruption of all other heads (Table 4). It also recovers the IOI circuit with a different, SAE-based method and scores agreement with the canonical circuit by ROC AUC. Both bear on V1 (faithfulness only) and V4. Its baseline AUCs (ACDC, HISP, SP) are cited from Conmy et al., not measured here.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add three points: the SAE circuit slightly underperforms the canonical ground-truth circuit (3.62 vs 4.11 logit diff); the baseline AUCs are taken from Conmy et al.; and the authors note that manually found ground-truth circuits may themselves be incomplete.
record.recipe_differences: The original study manually identified the IOI circuit using component interventions and causal analysis. This paper identifies heads using discrete SAE codes from positive and negative examples, then evaluates the predicted circuit by replacing activations outside it with corrupted activations.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI circuit-identification AUC varies across methods and random versus zero ablations. The authors also report lower IOI AUC when easy negatives are added and when unique positive codes are normalized by total unique codes per head; softmax across heads performs better than softmax across layers.

fits_no_version.finding: The SAE circuit-discovery method's IOI AUC drops with easy negatives, with softmax across layers, with code normalisation, and with more SAE training examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Performance of automated IOI circuit discovery depends on discovery-method design choices (data construction, normalisation).

record.code_released: The authors state that code will be released upon acceptance; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The study's predicted IOI circuit has 40 heads rather than the canonical 26 and does not test the claimed head-class roles by patching. The IOI circuit comparison reports inconsistent random-complement logit differences: -1.97 in Appendix B.1 text and -2.23 in Table 4. Several sensitivity results are presented only in figures without exact values.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted results for Greater-than, Docstring, Tracr, and induction because they do not directly test the IOI versions. Also omitted IOI faithfulness curves and other figure-only analyses not needed to document the direct circuit-performance and method-sensitivity findings recorded here.

untested.parts: Completeness and minimality; the seven head classes and their roles; faithfulness under the original mean ablation.
Entirely: no ablation of name movers and no measure of backup takeover.
Entirely for IOI. The induction results in Pythia and OPT concern a different task.
Agreement under ACDC/HISP/SP and across ablation types is only cited, not re-measured. EAP is compared on faithfulness curves only, not on overlap with the canonical circuit.
Not tested: there is no comparison of the canonical circuit's faithfulness or completeness across ablations, metrics or distributions.
Entirely: there is no variation of name order, templates or number of names.

missing.what: Which canonical heads the SAE circuit recovers: both negative name movers (L10H7, L11H10) and previous-token head L2H2, which ACDC reportedly missed. No position information is recovered.
Faithfulness curves (logit diff and KL) comparing EAP circuits with SAE circuits on IOI. Figure only; the SAE circuit matches or exceeds EAP.
A raw head-activation-difference baseline recovers the IOI circuit with AUC of about 0.80-0.85 at around 500 examples.

record.verdict_notes: Per-row links were changed, so the reader's guesses are revised: baseline AUCs are cited, and the R32-R34 sensitivity analyses concern the study's own method rather than the IOI circuit's evaluation. Hence there is no V5 verdict. The canonical circuit exceeding the full model (108%) under subject-swap corruption differs from the original paper's mean-ablation faithfulness, but the study makes no within-study comparison across ablations. The random-complement value is inconsistent (-1.97 in text vs -2.23 in the tables). Tranche is borderline T2/T4, since the paper mainly uses the canonical circuit as a benchmark for its method.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the roles of the seven head classes under patching, nor whether the original 26-head circuit itself meets faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. Its own predicted circuit contains 40 heads.
Backup name-mover heads are shown in a circuit diagram, but the study does not ablate main name-mover heads and test whether backups take over.

The study examines induction in other models, but does not test whether the IOI head classes and roles carry IOI in other models, sizes, or checkpoints, or whether IOI components are reused for other tasks.
Circuit-recovery AUC is compared across methods and ablations, but the study does not establish that the methods recover essentially identical circuits component by component.

The study reports sensitivity of IOI circuit-identification AUC to methods, ablation types, negative-example choices, and normalization choices. It does not establish that the IOI mechanism explains only part of the model's behaviour; its predicted circuit slightly exceeds the clean model on the reported logit-difference measure.
The IOI evaluation does not systematically vary name order, templates, or number of names.

relationships.condition: Canonical 26-head circuit in GPT-2 small, other heads patched with subject-swapped activations, logit-difference metric
relationships.reason: The circuit alone gives logit diff 4.11 (normalised 1.08) vs full model 3.55, so it carries the behaviour (R4, R9, R14). This covers faithfulness only.
relationships.display_finding: The circuit alone achieved a logit difference of 4.11, normalized to 1.08, versus 3.55 for the full model, demonstrating behavioral faithfulness.

relationships.condition: SAE-code circuit discovery on GPT-2 small IOI

relationships.display_finding: The 40-head circuit matched full-model performance at 3.62, but agreement with the canonical 26 heads reached AUC 0.84–0.86.
